posts.title: Hanuman Chalisa Meaning for Children, Part 1: The Opening Dohas and Chaupais 1 to 10, Line by Line
posts.description: A simple, line-by-line meaning of the Hanuman Chalisa for children, Part 1: the two opening dohas and chaupais 1 to 10, with our Kannada sing-along video, the stories behind the lines and why many families pray to Hanuman on Saturdays.

posts.title: Why Is Friday Lakshmi's Day? A Kannada Mahalakshmi Song and 8 Kinds of Wealth, Explained for Children
posts.description: Our Friday Kannada song Manege Baa Mahalakshmi, why many Indian homes pray to Goddess Lakshmi on Fridays, the eight kinds of wealth of the Ashtalakshmi, a short Sanskrit prayer with its meaning, and five Friday habits families can start today.

posts.title: Who Is Kadutha Swami? The Warrior Who Guards Sabarimala's 18 Holy Steps, Explained for Children
posts.description: The story of Kadutha Swami for children: the brave warrior who fought beside Manikanta, why his shrine stands at the foot of the 18 holy steps at Sabarimala with Karuppa Swami on the other side, what the 18 steps mean, and a lesson in loyalty.

posts.title: Just Right: Aarav's Seven Laddoos and Bhagavad Gita 6.17 on Balance, for Children
posts.description: Not too much, not too little. A short story about Aarav, seven laddoos and Grandpa's circle, what Bhagavad Gita 6.17 teaches about balance in eating, play, work and sleep, and one small step for families to try today.

posts.title: Why Did Manikanta Bring Tiger's Milk? The Ayyappa Tiger Story, Explained for Children
posts.description: The tiger's milk story of Ayyappa for children: Manikanta's guru dakshina, the queen's fear and pretend headache, the 12-year-old's walk into the forest, the tigers that bowed, the ride home to Pandalam and what it teaches about courage and forgiveness.

posts.title: Who Is Vavar Swami? How Ayyappa's Enemy Became His Best Friend, Explained for Children
posts.description: The story of Vavar Swami for children: the warrior from across the sea who fought Manikanta and became his lifelong friend, the Vavar mosque at Erumeli, Vavar Nada at Sabarimala, and a lesson in friendship.

posts.title: Who Is Malikappurathamma? The Story of the Devi Who Waits at Sabarimala, Explained for Children
posts.description: The story of Malikappurathamma for children: the maiden of light who rose after Mahishi fell, Manikanta's promise, why first-time pilgrims leave arrows at Sharamkuthi, and what the Devi who waits teaches us about patient love.

posts.title: Petta Thullal at Erumeli: Why Ayyappa Pilgrims Dance With Colours, Explained for Children
posts.description: What the Petta Thullal dance at Erumeli is, how it remembers Manikanta's victory over Mahishi, why pilgrims visit Vavar's shrine on the way, and what children can learn from it, explained for families.

posts.title: What Is Mala Dharana? The 41-Day Ayyappa Mandala Vratham Explained for Children
posts.description: Why Ayyappa devotees wear a mala for 41 days, what the Mandala vratham asks of them, who a Kanni Swami is, and simple ways children can join the season at home, explained for families.

posts.title: Be the Example: Riya's Shoes and Bhagavad Gita 3.21 for Children
posts.description: Children copy what we do, not what we say. A short story about a big sister and a row of shoes, what Bhagavad Gita 3.21 teaches about setting an example, and one quiet habit to try today.

posts.title: Swamiye Saranam Ayyappa Meaning for Children: Why Every Sabarimala Pilgrim Is Called 'Swami'
posts.description: What 'Swamiye Saranam Ayyappa' means, word by word, why pilgrims chant it as a call and answer, why they call each other Swami, and the 'Tattvamasi' lesson at Sabarimala, explained simply for children and families.

posts.title: What Is the Irumudi? Ayyappa's Sacred Two-Part Bundle Explained for Children
posts.description: Why Sabarimala pilgrims carry an irumudi on their heads: the two parts, the ghee-filled coconut, the Kettu Nira ceremony and the lesson inside, explained simply for children and families.

posts.title: This Will Pass: Kabir's Cold Pool and Bhagavad Gita 2.14 for Children
posts.description: A short story of a boy's first swimming lesson, what Bhagavad Gita 2.14 teaches about cold and heat, joy and pain that come and go, and one small step for children and families.

posts.title: The Story of Ayyappa for Children: Manikanta, the Tiger and the 18 Steps of Sabarimala
posts.description: A simple telling of the Ayyappa story for children and families: baby Manikanta at Pandalam, the ride on the tigress, the 41-day vratham and the 18 sacred steps of Sabarimala.

posts.title: Pampa to Kuvempu: 6 Great Kannada Poets Every Child Should Know
posts.description: A simple guide for children and families to six great Kannada poets, from Adikavi Pampa and Basavanna to Akka Mahadevi, Sarvajna, Bendre and Kuvempu, with our Rajyotsava song.

posts.title: Lift Yourself: Meera's Bicycle and Bhagavad Gita 6.5 for Children
posts.description: A short story of a girl learning to ride a bicycle, what Bhagavad Gita 6.5 says about the mind as our best friend or worst enemy, and one small step for children and families.

posts.title: Steady Hands in the Storm: The Potter, Calm Action and Bhagavad Gita 2.48
posts.description: A short story of a potter who keeps his hands steady in a storm, what Bhagavad Gita 2.48 says about samatvam (evenness of mind), and one calm-action step for children and families.

posts.title: Bali Padyami Story for Children: King Bali, Vamana and the Promise of Three Steps
posts.description: The story of King Bali and Vamana told for children, why Bali Padyami is celebrated after Deepavali in Karnataka and Maharashtra, its link with Onam, and a simple promise activity for families.

posts.title: Why Do We Light Diyas on Deepavali? Rama's Return to Ayodhya, Told for Children
posts.description: The story of Rama's return to Ayodhya, why Deepavali means a row of lamps, the five days of the festival, and a simple diya activity for children and parents.

posts.title: Run From Fear and It Chases You: Swami Vivekananda, the Monkeys and Bhagavad Gita 2.3
posts.description: The story of Swami Vivekananda and the monkeys of Banaras, what Bhagavad Gita 2.3 says about fear, and one small step children and parents can take today.
